cards.title: Introduction to Spring Boot Deployment
cards.content:
Spring Boot makes deployment easy because it comes with an embedded servlet container (like Tomcat or Jetty). You don't need to manually set up an external application server.

Common deployment targets include executable JAR files, Docker containers, and Cloud platforms like AWS, Heroku, or GCP.

cards.title: JAR vs WAR Packaging
cards.content:
By default, Spring Boot projects are packaged as JAR files, running via java -jar app.jar.

You can also configure your project to build a WAR file if you need to deploy it to a traditional external application server.

cards.title: Running the Application
cards.content: To run a Spring Boot packaged application from the command line, you use the command: java [blank] application.jar

cards.title: Containerization with Docker
cards.content:
Docker allows you to package your Spring Boot application along with its runtime environment into a container.

FROM eclipse-temurin:17-jre
VOLUME /tmp
COPY target/*.jar app.jar
ENTRYPOINT ["java","-jar","/app.jar"]

Build the Docker image using 'docker build'

cards.title: Environment Profiles
cards.content:
Profiles help segregate configuration parts of your application and make them available only in certain environments.

You can activate a profile using spring.profiles.active=prod in your application.properties or via command line arguments: --spring.profiles.active=prod.

cards.title: Cloud Deployment Options
cards.content:
Spring Boot applications can be easily deployed to modern cloud providers:

  • AWS Elastic Beanstalk / ECS: For containerized or raw jar deployments.
  • Google Cloud Run: Excellent for serverless container deployments.
  • Heroku: Quick deployment using buildpacks.
